meta.title: Muse introduction (Meta app launch film)
meta.note: bin/dissect found 6 hard cuts; this is a motion-graphics film whose real units are beats joined by zooms, morphs and punch-ins, so the 6 measured shots are split into 37 beats at frame-difference peaks. Measured fields (brightness, colour, change, loudness) were re-measured per beat with the same method.

acts.name: Reveal
acts.function: Brand open: app icon pulls back into a world of everyday 3D objects, then kinetic type names the product and the category ("Muse is your personal AI agent", "A new kind of AI").

acts.name: Demo 1: school supplies
acts.function: A hectic week, one prompt; the agent reads an email, builds a cart and asks permission; the user taps Allow; "Done!". Teaches the loop: ask -> agent works (status pill) -> permission -> done.

acts.name: Benefit carousel 1
acts.function: "AI that ___ for you" with four swaps on the beat.

acts.name: Demo 2: race sign-up
acts.function: Proactive agent: reads training data, suggests a 10K, fills a web form in a browser, submits; payoff on the mascot running through confetti as the chorus drops.

acts.name: Benefit carousel 2
acts.function: Four more "AI that ___ for you" swaps.

acts.name: Demo 3: flight delay
acts.function: Agent notices a delay, checks options, asks one question, rebooks to the next day; payoff "Your Muse gets it done" with confetti.

acts.name: Benefit carousel 3 + integrations
acts.function: Last swaps, then "Connect your apps" -> "All in one place".

acts.name: Brand close
acts.function: Mirror of the open ("It's your Muse" in the object grid), trust lines ("keeps you up-to-date / in the loop / in control"), black end card with store badges and Meta logo.

look.grade: Clean high-key digital: off-white #F4F7FA fields, cool and neutral, the only saturated colour is royal blue #1A6CF0 (brand, buttons, checks, selection) plus small emoji accents; one yellow (training card) and one red (Delayed bar) accent.
look.contrast: Low-contrast fields with high-contrast black type; no blacks except the final end card and the browser bezel in shot 21.
look.light: No physical lighting: flat fields; UI elements carry very soft diffuse drop shadows; title cards have a pale sky-blue glow rising from the bottom edge (strongest bottom-right); UI scenes have a soft grey diagonal shade to the bottom-right.
look.depth_of_field: Everything sharp, except one rack-focus (shot 29, calendar blurs in) and motion blur on fast scrolls and zooms.
look.brightness_range: Shots 1-36 sit at 187-252 (most 230-248); the darkest moment is the browser/Submit pair at 187-218 (shots 21-22); the end card sits at 6-7.
look.mascot_render: The mascot and the emoji objects are soft, slightly glossy 3D renders (plush fleece texture for the mascot) dropped into flat 2D graphics.

text_style.typeface: Friendly geometric-humanist sans (Meta-house style; e.g. a rounded grotesk such as Inter Display or Figtree as stand-in), medium weight for headlines, regular for UI.
text_style.case: Sentence case everywhere; "TRAINING PLAN ADJUSTED" is the only all-caps label.
text_style.size: Measured on 1920x1080 frames: headlines cap height 9.5-10.5% H (~150 px type); carousel middle line ~60 px (cap 4.6% H); wide chat text 36 px (cap 2.4% H); macro chat 80 px (cap 5.4% H); 'It's your Muse' cap 11% H shrinking to 4.2% H. The earlier '90-110 px' figure was about 0.6x too small.
text_style.colour: Black #1C1E21 on light fields; brand word "Muse" in royal blue #1A6CF0 in shot 2; white on black at the end.
text_style.position: Always horizontally centred; blocks sit slightly above the middle (centre at about 45% height).
text_style.animation: Words pop in one at a time on the beat or half-beat (scale 80% -> 105% -> 100% with fade, about 6 frames, overshoot ease); 3D emoji pop into reserved gaps between words; chat text types word by word; swaps exit upward; "Done!" letters bounce on a wavy baseline.

sound.music: One licensed-style upbeat pop/hip-hop track with a sung/rapped lead vocal, 115 BPM (beat 0.521 s, first beat at 0.08 s, bar 2.08 s). The edit follows it: text swaps and pops land on beats and half-beats.

sound.mix: Score only, mastered loud and steady (-15 LUFS in the chorus). No separate UI sound effects were measured; if added, keep them subtle under the music.
